newsitem.title: JAPAN: Marubeni to enter satellite broadcasting.
newsitem.headline: Marubeni to enter satellite broadcasting.

text.p: Japan's Marubeni Corp is to spend up to 30 billion yen ($250 million) to enter the satellite broadcasting industry, a company spokesman said on Saturday.

"Over the next two years we will be investing up to 30 billion yen. Around half will go towards setting up programme production companies and the rest will be towards other investments, although the figure is still fluid," the Marubeni spokesman told Reuters.

He was commenting on a report in the Nihon Keizai Shimbun newspaper which said Marubeni was considering whether to take a stake in the satellite broadcasting venture, Japan Sky Broadcasting Corp (JSkyB).

The spokesman said it was less likely that Marubeni would join JSkyB, media giant News Corp's Japanese satellite venture, because of the possible involvement of companies like Sony Corp and Fuji Television Network.
"If Fuji enters JSkyB then it's likely Sony will also join in. That would mean the chances of Marubeni also joining will be slim," he said.
"From our point of view, the fewer shareholders each with a large stake the better."
